solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Close to nothing in charity that's opening

indicators.note: in says the zero letter goes inside the word for charity

parts.note: alms are gifts given to the poor, so charity
the round figure zero looks like the letter O

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here the first of that's

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a charity is opening with almost no money behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean nearly or not quite, as in close to midnight or almost midnight.

clue.text: Unaware of past uprising as some of America is, en masse

indicators.note: uprising says the hidden letters are read backwards
some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A political jibe that much of America has forgotten its own history as it rises up together.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'uprising' reads the hidden run CAISENMA from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone suffering memory loss knows nothing of what happened before, so is unaware of the past.

clue.text: Principal substituting old boy for a family man

indicators.note: substituting with for says one set of letters is swapped in where the other was

parts.note: the master is the head of a school or college, its principal
OB is the usual abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A school head is replaced by a former pupil in place of a family man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Family' is the Mafia sense: a crime family, so its member is a gangster.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangster belongs to a crime family in Mafia slang, so he is a family man in a cryptic sense.

clue.text: Rolling fat?

parts.note: a roll of fat round the waist, and the backup wheel a car rolls on

explanation.walkthrough: A spare tyre is slang for a roll of fat around the waist, and a tyre is something that rolls.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a bulge of flab around the middle, punning on the extra wheel carried in a car's boot.

clue.text: Jazzy music involving musical sense is promising

indicators.note: involving says one piece takes in the other

parts.note: swing is a style of big-band jazz
an ear for music is a musical sense

explanation.surface: Jazz that shows a good ear is full of promise.
explanation.definitionFit: Swearing an oath is vowing or pledging, the same act as promising.

clue.text: Gentle champion's stopping stock conflicts

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so these pieces sit inside the word for stock

parts.note: wares are a shop's stock of goods
gentle means soft
a champion is a hero, so champion's gives hero's

explanation.surface: A mild-mannered champion stepping in to halt fights over goods.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifteenth-century English civil wars between York and Lancaster, a series of conflicts.

clue.text: Reason males are excluded from rummage around

indicators.note: around says the remaining letters are moved about into a new order
are excluded from says those letters are taken out of the next word

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male, so males gives two of them

explanation.surface: A shop where men are banned from searching through the jumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are excluded from' strips both Ms from RUMMAGE to leave RUAGE, which 'around' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To reason with someone or reason a case is to present a logical case, a verb sense of the same act.

clue.text: Man in promise to pay on time shows resolve

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed after what goes before
in says the man's name goes inside the debt note

parts.note: an IOU is a written promise to pay a debt
Ron is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man paying his debt promptly proves his determination.
explanation.definitionFit: To smooth out a difficulty is to settle or resolve it, an idiom from pressing creases flat.

clue.text: Most like The Merry Widow being terribly stagey

indicators.note: terribly suggests something done badly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A review panning a production of Lehar's operetta as hammy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Merry Widow' is Lehar's operetta; merry gives the old sense of gay, cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Gay in its older sense means merry, so whatever is most merry is most like a merry widow.

clue.text: Peace group requests soldiers possibly to protect brief retreat in quarrel

parts.note: the UN, United Nations, is a peacekeeping body
pleas are requests

indicators.note: to protect means to surround and shield, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: soldier ants are a caste of ant, so soldiers might be ants

indicators.note: brief says the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a nest is a cosy retreat or hideaway

explanation.surface: A long-winded account of a peacekeeping body asking troops to cover a withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soldiers possibly' is a definition by example: soldier ants are one caste of ant, flagged by 'possibly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpleasantness is a euphemism for a row or quarrel, as in the recent unpleasantness.

clue.text: Trivial problem to fall between aristocrat and monarch

indicators.note: between puts one piece in the middle of the two others

parts.note: a nob is slang for a toff or aristocrat
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
rain means to fall from the sky

explanation.surface: A minor puzzle about falling down between a nobleman and a king.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a decision so easy it needs no thought, so a trivial problem.

clue.text: Crack from unknown imbecile

parts.note: to have a crack is to have a go
of can mean from, as in a man of Kent
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A wisecrack from an unidentified idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Goofy is an adjective meaning silly or foolish, so it describes an imbecile.

clue.text: Desirable quality in grand name of literary siblings

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: swell is an old-fashioned word for grand or excellent
it is sex appeal, a desirable quality, as in the It girl

explanation.surface: Praising the attractive trait in a great literary family name.
explanation.walkthrough: Edith, Osbert and Sacheverell Sitwell were a famous trio of English writers.
explanation.definitionFit: Surname of the three English writer siblings Edith, Osbert and Sacheverell.

clue.text: Oppressive old tyrant leading America

indicators.note: leading says the tyrant goes in front of the country

parts.note: Nero was a tyrannical Roman emperor
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A despot of old leading the United States would be harsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Onerous means burdensome or heavy to bear, so oppressive.

clue.text: Marshal calm when changing side repeatedly

indicators.note: changing side twice means the left letters each become right ones

parts.note: to allay fears is to calm them

explanation.surface: A field marshal staying calm as he switches sides again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: L and R stand for left and right; both Ls of ALLAY become Rs.
explanation.definitionFit: To marshal troops is to arrange them in order, a verb sense of the same idea.

clue.text: A diet not designed as a remedy

indicators.note: designed means made up to a new plan, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A meal plan not intended to cure anything.
explanation.definitionFit: An antidote counters a poison, so it is a cure or remedy.

clue.text: Outlaw's unfeeling ring captures northbound travellers

indicators.note: captures says the outer pieces hold the travellers inside

parts.note: dead to sensation means unfeeling

indicators.note: in a down clue northbound means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: reps are commercial travellers, travelling salesmen
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted gang ambushing salesmen heading north, like a Wild West bandit.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless criminal of the Wild West, an outlaw.

clue.text: Complaint caused by command from detective?

parts.note: DI is a detective inspector, and from the detective gives the possessive DI's
an order is a command

explanation.surface: A grievance arising from an instruction a police officer gave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'command from detective' is read as the detective's order: DI'S ORDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical complaint is an illness or ailment, the same as a disorder.

clue.text: Line that stops tongue moving, twisted in knots?

definitions.text: Line that stops tongue moving, twisted in knots?

parts.words: Line that stops tongue moving, twisted in knots?
parts.note: a cord that holds down the tongue of a shoe and is tied in bows

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a tongue-tied speaker; the tongue is a shoe's flap and the line is a cord tied in knots.
explanation.definitionFit: The cord threaded through a shoe's eyelets keeps its flap in place and is tied in a bow.

clue.text: Crop top with short dart in front

indicators.note: in front says the shortened word goes before the garment
short says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to hare is to run fast, to dart
a vest is a top, an upper garment

explanation.surface: A cropped top with a short tuck sewn at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crop top' looks like one garment; crop is the definition and top gives VEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A harvest is the gathered crop of a season.

clue.text: Cold dish using incomplete vessels (below and above water)

indicators.note: incomplete says each vessel loses its last letter

parts.note: a sub sails below the water and a ship above it

explanation.surface: A chilled meal served on a variety of plates and bowls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' cuts SUB to SU and SHIP to SHI.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is Japanese vinegared rice with raw fish, served cold.

clue.text: Vegetable: wrap up portion

parts.note: wrap up is slang for be quiet, which sh also says
to portion out is to allot

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction to parcel up a helping of vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrap up' is British slang for shut up, hence SH.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallot is a small onion-like bulb, a vegetable.

clue.text: I caught summer in Paris on a refresher

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed after

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
ete is French for summer

explanation.surface: A tourist in Paris for the summer catches a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold sweet tea is a drink that refreshes, so a refresher.

clue.text: Something ideal for jamming broadcast, in short

indicators.note: in says one word goes inside the other

parts.note: curt means short in manner
a station ran a story means it broadcast it

explanation.surface: Talk of a device for blocking radio signals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jamming' suggests radio interference; here it is making jam.
explanation.definitionFit: Small dried or fresh berries such as blackcurrants are a classic fruit for making jam.

clue.text: Heel's neighbour caused anger after undressing

indicators.note: undressing strips the outer layer, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: rankled means irritated or caused anger

explanation.surface: A neighbour who is a heel stirred up resentment after stripping off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heel' looks like a cad; it is the back of the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The joint just above the back of the foot sits right beside it, so is its neighbour.

clue.text: Men concerned with later life backing part of Mediterranean diet?

parts.note: OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers or men

indicators.note: backing says those letters are read backwards

parts.note: on means about or concerned with
age is the later part of life

explanation.surface: Men worried about old age go back to a healthy southern European diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is a herb widely used in Italian and Greek cooking, so it features in that diet.

clue.text: Trader's tip diluted small change

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter

parts.note: diluted drinks are weak

explanation.surface: A stockbroker's advice was watered down with a minor adjustment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small change' wants to be coins; it is a slight adjustment.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweak is a slight adjustment or modification.

clue.text: Watched and heard the writer with no hair

indicators.note: heard says the words are said aloud to give the answer

parts.note: the writer refers to themself as I, and with no hair is bald

explanation.surface: A bald author was watched and listened to.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball someone is to stare at or watch them closely.

clue.text: Theatrical set, scary in play

indicators.note: in play means moving about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dramatic stage set designed to be frightening in a production.
explanation.definitionFit: Actressy describes showy behaviour like a stage performer, so theatrical or affected.

clue.text: Short cannon's middle-of-the-road rating

parts.note: MOR is the music-trade abbreviation for middle-of-the-road
a rating is an ordinary sailor, a tar

explanation.surface: Assessing a cannon as average.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortar is a short-barrelled cannon firing shells at a high angle.
